crossRefs.note: When I wept and I fasted, that was to my reproach.
When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword to them.
Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy?
But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who…
Bless those who persecute you; bless, and don’t curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
“It shall be a statute to you forever: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your…
It is a Sabbath of solemn rest to you, and you shall afflict your souls. It is a statute forever.

‘Why have we fasted,’ they say, ‘and you don’t see? Why have we afflicted our soul, and you don’t notice?’ “Behold, in…
Is this the fast that I have chosen? A day for a man to humble his soul? Is it to bow down his head like a reed, and to…
Then John’s disciples came to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples don’t fast?”
Jesus said to them, “Can the friends of the bridegroom mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will…
If the household is worthy, let your peace come on it, but if it isn’t worthy, let your peace return to you.
If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; but if not, it will return to you.

translations.web: But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth. I afflicted my soul with fasting. My prayer returned into my own bosom.
translations.bsb: Yet when they were ill, I put on sackcloth; I humbled myself with fasting, but my prayers returned unanswered.
translations.kjv: But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth: I humbled my soul with fasting; and my prayer returned into mine own bosom.
translations.asv: But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth: I afflicted my soul with fasting; And my prayer returned into mine own bosom.
